s: Which Buddhist site in Andhra Pradesh is known for rock-cut caves, stupas and monastic remains?
Which of the following Stupas is the biggest in Andhra Pradesh?
x:
The Amaravati Stupa, also known as the Mahachaitya, is the largest Buddhist Stupa in Andhra Pradesh and one of the most magnificent Buddhist monuments in India. Originally constructed during the Satavahana period and enlarged under the Ikshvakus, the stupa became an important centre of Mahayana Buddhism. It was renowned for its exquisitely carved limestone railings, sculptured panels and narrative reliefs depicting scenes from the life of the Buddha and Jataka stories. The Amaravati School of Art, which developed around this monument, is internationally recognized for its artistic excellence and had a profound influence on Buddhist art in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia. Although important stupas also exist at Bhattiprolu, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda, the Amaravati Stupa is the largest among them.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Largest Buddhist Stupa in Andhra Pradesh – Amaravati Mahachaitya
Famous For – Amaravati School of Art

s: The stupas and viharas at Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda were built over whose relics?
x:
The famous Buddhist monuments at Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda are relic stupas, constructed to enshrine the sacred relics of Gautama Buddha. These centres flourished under the patronage of the Satavahanas and later the Ikshvakus. Excavations have revealed relic caskets, Buddhist sculptures, inscriptions, monasteries (Viharas), Chaityas and beautifully carved limestone panels depicting the life of Buddha and Jataka stories. These sites became internationally renowned centres of Mahayana Buddhism and attracted monks and pilgrims from Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
n: Built over relics of Gautama Buddha
